findings.claim: The 25:8 to 25:9 seam carries a byte-true legal-dispute catchword this row never discloses, and the row rejects the 25:8-9 cluster on a 'too pervasive' threshold it applies inconsistently with its own neighbouring cluster rows.
findings.grounds: Byte facts at the row's right seam: 25:8 and 25:9 share 2 exact skeleton tokens (reekha plus the negative particle, the particle being pervasive at 78 verses book-wide and carrying nothing), and beyond the token the root r-y-b straddles the seam, לָרִ֗ב (oshb:Prov.25.8), word-bound at exactly 1 verse book-wide, against רִֽ֭יבְךָ רִ֣יב (oshb:Prov.25.9), the two verses being one lawsuit scene. The 25:9 row discloses that same root link at the same seam; this row discloses only reekha, so the standing cross-seam cohesion rule (a byte-true device straddling the row's own seam argues continuity unless disclosed) is met asymmetrically. The rejection ground is also internally inconsistent: 4 verses in an 83-verse work unit, 2 of them the adjacent pair under test, is called 'too pervasive to bound a two-verse unit', while the same run clusters oshb:Prov.25.2-Prov.25.3 on 2 shared tokens and oshb:Prov.25.11-Prov.25.12 on 1 shared content token plus adjacency. The row's warrant is not byte-false, so no respan is proposed here; a 25:8-9 cluster is nevertheless the live alternative for adjudication.

findings.claim: The atomic row severs a verse-initial subordinate pen-clause from the governing prohibition standing in the previous verse, and the row's stated warrant never reaches the subordinator.
findings.grounds: oshb:Prov.25.10 opens with פֶּֽן, a subordinating particle, and contains no governing clause; its governing prohibition אַל תְּגָֽל stands in oshb:Prov.25.9. This is not a punctuation argument: the particle is in the MT bytes. Book-wide byte control: exactly 7 Prov verses open with pen (Prov.5.9, Prov.5.10, Prov.22.25, Prov.24.18, Prov.25.10, Prov.30.9, Prov.31.5; sweep: 7 verses), and in all 7 the governing clause stands in the PREVIOUS verse, while the pen clauses of oshb:Prov.25.8, oshb:Prov.25.16 and oshb:Prov.25.17 all sit inside their own verse. The row's warrant, that the verse 'introduces its own subject and predicate', is true of the clause internally, יְחַסֶּדְךָ֥ שֹׁמֵ֑עַ (oshb:Prov.25.10), but does not make a pen clause an independent unit. The owner S6 ruled precedent B-10, that a syntactically continuous single sentence spanning two verses is ONE proverb-unit typed single_proverb regardless of verse count, is directly on point. On file as the counter-argument: the 25:9 row reads the dependency as 'a warning appended after an already-complete instruction rather than a syntactic requirement for v9 to parse', which tests v9's parsability, not whether v10 can stand as a unit.
findings.proposed_change: PROPOSAL for adjudication: merge into one single_proverb row spanning Prov.25.9-Prov.25.10, respanning the 25:9 row to Prov.25.9-Prov.25.10 and retiring this row, with the pen subordination named as the byte warrant and the B-10 precedent cited. Dependent fields to re-open on the swap: observed_substrate_signals, unit_type, strongest_rejected_alternative, confidence.

findings.claim: Both cola of 25:10 are mis-glossed in the boundary_rationale.
findings.grounds: The rationale renders the verse as 'a hearer's report and a reputation that never returns'. Colon 1, יְחַסֶּדְךָ֥ שֹׁמֵ֑עַ (oshb:Prov.25.10), has the hearer SHAME the addressee, not report it: WEB reads “lest one who hears it put you to shame” (web:Prov.25.10). Colon 2, וְ֝דִבָּתְךָ֗ לֹ֣א תָשֽׁוּב (oshb:Prov.25.10), is the ill-repute not DEPARTING, not a good name failing to return: WEB reads “your bad reputation never depart” (web:Prov.25.10). The row's own device_notes gets the effect right ('irrecoverable reputation'), so this is prose only and does no boundary work.
findings.proposed_change: Field repair, boundary_rationale: re-gloss colon 1 as the hearer shaming the addressee and colon 2 as the ill-repute that does not depart.

findings.claim: The strongest_rejected_alternative's sole ground is byte-false as to 25:17: the two verses do share an exact skeleton token, plus a shared root and a shared construction, and none of it is disclosed.
findings.grounds: The row states 'No merge with 25:15 or 25:17 was warranted; both are topically unrelated and share no skeleton token with this verse.' The 25:15 half is true (25:15 to 25:16 shows 0 shared exact skeleton tokens). The 25:17 half is false: 25:16 and 25:17 share the exact skeleton token pen, byte-identical in both verses, פֶּן (oshb:Prov.25.16) and פֶּן (oshb:Prov.25.17). Beyond the token they share the sin-bet-ayin root in the same slot, תִּ֝שְׂבָּעֶ֗נּוּ (oshb:Prov.25.16) against יִ֝שְׂבָּעֲךָ֗ (oshb:Prov.25.17), and the pen-plus-suffixed-yiqtol construction built on that root stands at exactly 4 verses book-wide (Prov.5.10, Prov.25.16, Prov.25.17, Prov.30.9; sweep: 4 verses), of which oshb:Prov.25.16 and oshb:Prov.25.17 are the ONLY adjacent pair. Both verses are admonitions against having too much of a thing. Nothing of this straddling device is disclosed here, while the 25:17 row does disclose the sin-bet-ayin root at the same seam. Load-bearing: this sentence is the entire stated warrant for rejecting the strongest rival, and a shared construction run is one of the owner gate's named cluster warrants for C5; the same run clusters oshb:Prov.25.11-Prov.25.12 on 1 shared content token plus adjacency, a thinner case than this one. Confidence high is correspondingly over-stated.
findings.proposed_change: PROPOSAL for adjudication, either arm: (a) replace the dead warrant with one that survives the true bytes, a replacement having to pass the test that killed the original, and disclose the pen and sin-bet-ayin construction straddling the 25:16 to 25:17 seam; or (b) respan Prov.25.16-Prov.25.17 as one proverb_cluster on the shared construction run, retiring the 25:17 atomic row. Dependent fields to re-open either way: observed_substrate_signals, device_notes, unit_type, confidence.

findings.claim: The verse's opening colon is labelled a rhetorical question on the strength of WEB punctuation; the MT carries no interrogative marker.
findings.grounds: boundary_rationale opens 'A rhetorical question-then-warning about honey' and device_notes repeats 'a question followed by its own warning clause'. The MT reads דְּבַ֣שׁ מָ֭צָאתָ (oshb:Prov.25.16), a bare noun-plus-qatal clause with no interrogative particle; the question is supplied by WEB, “Have you found honey?” (web:Prov.25.16), that is by tier-4 translation punctuation, which is never boundary evidence. Corroborative rather than driving, so low: the row's intra-verse completeness is byte-visible without the label, and the parallelism class in device_notes is texture by rule. Contrast oshb:Prov.25.8, where פֶּ֣ן מַה puts a real interrogative in the Hebrew, so the same form label is byte-grounded there and not here.
findings.proposed_change: Field repair, boundary_rationale plus device_notes: describe the colon from the Hebrew (a circumstantial 'you have found honey' clause, however WEB renders it) or mark the interrogative reading explicitly as a tier-4 WEB rendering carrying no weight.
